Daily Brief

The most significant diplomatic development today emerged from Abu Dhabi, where US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine yielded agreement on what Jared Kushner called the 'biggest humanitarian release of prisoners' in the conflict's history [The Hindu, Globe and Mail, BBC]. US envoys Kushner and Witkoff will travel to Moscow Thursday to meet President Putin before briefing President Zelensky in Dublin. Meanwhile, Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years as millions of workers protested the housing crisis ahead of a crucial national election [The Hindu, Globe and Mail, Le Monde]. COP31 opened in Antalya with notable absences—only UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham among G7 leaders is scheduled to address the summit, while French President Macron cited Armistice Day commemorations [RFI, Globe and Mail]. In Washington, the House of Representatives blocked a Republican-led effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over unauthorized military action against Iran, though Democrats signaled they may revisit the matter when they assume control of Congress in January [BBC, France 24]. Across Europe, coordinated bomb threats targeted hundreds of schools in Italy, Scotland, and Ireland, with Italian Prime Minister Meloni convening an emergency security meeting [BBC, Financial Times].

01 Geopolitics

Russia and Ukraine Agree to Largest Prisoner Exchange of War After US-Brokered Talks in Abu Dhabi

  • US envoy Jared Kushner announced agreement on the 'biggest humanitarian release of prisoners' after two days of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, with final numbers to be confirmed Thursday
  • Both Russian delegation head Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov confirmed the planned large-scale exchange
  • Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow Thursday to meet President Putin, then to Dublin to brief President Zelensky
  • President Zelensky, speaking from Paris, described the first day of talks as 'constructive and quite substantive,' though no breakthrough on ending the war was achieved

02 Economics

Spain Stages First General Strike in 14 Years Over Housing Crisis Ahead of National Election

  • Millions of workers walked out under the slogan 'Salaries. Housing. Prices.' causing widespread transport disruption and business closures across the country
  • Major unions UGT and CCOO reported participation rates of 90% in automotive and port sectors, 85% in meat industry, 82% in waste collection, and 75% in energy
  • Average rent in Spain has nearly doubled over the past decade, fueling public anger ahead of elections that could bring the far right to power
  • Minor clashes occurred in Barcelona with roadblocks and burning tires, while police used pepper spray against protesters in Madrid

03 Climate

COP31 Opens in Turkey with G7 Leaders Largely Absent as Climate Takes Backseat to Global Conflicts

  • UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is the only G7 leader scheduled to address the summit in Antalya, Turkey
  • French President Macron, German Chancellor Merz, and Italian PM Meloni are all absent, along with Canadian and Japanese prime ministers
  • Brazilian President Lula criticized the international community for talking 'more about weapons and tariffs than the survival of future generations'
  • Turkish President Erdogan and EU chief Ursula von der Leyen are attending, with leaders warning wars and trade disputes must not distract from climate action

US House Blocks Effort to Impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth Over Iran Military Action

  • Republican congressman Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of waging war on Iran without congressional authorization
  • House voted along party lines to refer the resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively killing the effort for now
  • Hegseth called the impeachment bid a 'farce' and 'sabotage' in his first Pentagon briefing in six months
  • House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries warned 'This is not the end of it' as Democrats prepare to assume control of Congress in January

Coordinated Bomb Threats Target Hundreds of Schools Across Italy, Scotland and Ireland

  • Approximately 300 schools across Italy received bomb threats via email, prompting evacuations in Rome, Naples, Florence and other cities
  • Italian Education Minister described incidents as likely a 'cyber-attack, not a genuine risk' with a clear strategy behind the threats
  • Prime Minister Meloni convened emergency meeting of ministers and intelligence chiefs, stating no evidence of 'concrete danger'
